events.title: Queen Elizabeth I Dies, Ending the Tudor Era
events.description: Elizabeth I died at Richmond Palace after more than 44 years on the throne. She left no children. James VI of Scotland succeeded her as James I of England.
events.significance: Her death ended the Tudor dynasty and united the English and Scottish crowns under one monarch. That union was a major step toward the creation of Great Britain.

events.title: Robert Koch Announces the Cause of Tuberculosis
events.description: German physician Robert Koch announced that he had identified the bacterium that causes tuberculosis. At the time, the disease was one of the deadliest in the world.
events.significance: The discovery helped establish modern bacteriology and made diagnosis and treatment research possible. Koch won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1905.

events.title: Archbishop Óscar Romero Is Assassinated
events.description: Salvadoran Archbishop Óscar Romero was shot dead while celebrating Mass in San Salvador. He had been an outspoken critic of human rights abuses during the build-up to El Salvador's civil war.
events.significance: His killing became a global symbol of the struggle for human rights and justice. He was later canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church.

events.title: Exxon Valdez Runs Aground in Alaska
events.description: The oil tanker Exxon Valdez struck a reef in Prince William Sound, Alaska. The crash spilled millions of gallons of crude oil into the pristine waters.
events.significance: It was one of the most devastating environmental disasters in history, killing vast numbers of seabirds and other wildlife. It led to tougher US oil-transport safety laws.
